html:
The Quinisext Council was a church council held in Constantinople in 692 under Emperor Justinian II. It is also called the Council in Trullo, after the domed hall of the palace where it met. Its name means "fifth-sixth": it issued the church rules that the fifth and sixth councils, such as the council of 680, had not made.

It passed 102 canons on church life, covering the clergy, marriage, fasting, feasts and how Christ should be shown in art. Some went against Roman custom. It allowed married men to become priests and keep their wives, forbade fasting on the Saturdays of Lent, and confirmed the see of Constantinople as equal in privileges to Rome, though second in rank.

Pope Sergius I refused to sign the canons, and Justinian's attempt to arrest him failed when soldiers in Italy protected him. The Orthodox churches still follow its rules. It was one of the many small differences that slowly pulled the Latin West and Greek East apart before the schism of 1054.
